tags.label: Single point of failure
tags.description: Only one instance carries this responsibility, so losing it takes down everything downstream.

tags.label: No backup
tags.description: No copy of this data exists elsewhere, so any corruption or deletion is permanent.

tags.label: Single availability zone
tags.description: All resources live in one availability zone, so a zonal failure takes the entire component offline.

tags.label: Single region
tags.description: All resources live in one cloud region, so a regional disaster eliminates every redundant path.

tags.label: Unencrypted
tags.description: Data is stored or transmitted in plaintext, exposing it to anyone who can read the underlying medium.

tags.label: Publicly exposed
tags.description: The endpoint is reachable from the public internet without network-level restrictions, widening the attack surface.

tags.label: No rate limit
tags.description: Unlimited inbound traffic is accepted, so a surge or malicious flood can exhaust capacity instantly.

tags.label: No autoscaling
tags.description: Capacity is fixed at provisioning time, so unexpected load will saturate the component and cause errors.

tags.label: Manual failover
tags.description: Switching to a standby requires human intervention, so the outage lasts as long as it takes someone to act.

tags.label: No monitoring
tags.description: No metrics or traces are collected, so failures are invisible until users report them.

tags.label: No alerting
tags.description: Even if metrics exist, no alerts fire when thresholds are breached, leaving the team unaware of ongoing incidents.

tags.label: Stale TLS certificate
tags.description: The TLS certificate is expired or near expiry, causing clients to reject connections with a hard error.

tags.label: Cold cache
tags.description: The cache has been emptied, so every request falls through to the datastore behind it and latency spikes.

tags.label: Unbounded queue
tags.description: The message queue has no depth limit or consumer throttle, so a backlog grows without bound until memory is exhausted.

tags.label: No dead-letter queue
tags.description: A message that cannot be processed has nowhere to go, so it is retried forever or lost, and the failure is invisible.

tags.label: Shared credentials
tags.description: Multiple services or users share the same secret, so a single credential leak compromises all of them simultaneously.

tags.label: No rollback capability
tags.description: Deployments cannot be reversed automatically, so a bad release requires a full re-deploy that prolongs the outage.

tags.label: Untested restore
tags.description: Backups exist but have never been successfully restored, so recovery procedures are unvalidated and may fail under pressure.

tags.label: Vertically scalable only
tags.description: Capacity can only be increased by upgrading the instance size, which has a hard ceiling and requires downtime.

tags.label: Has replica
tags.description: A second copy exists and can absorb reads or be promoted during a primary failure.

tags.label: Auto failover
tags.description: The system detects primary failure and promotes a standby automatically, minimising the recovery time objective.

tags.label: Multi-AZ
tags.description: Resources are spread across multiple availability zones, so a single zonal outage does not cause a full service interruption.

tags.label: Multi-region
tags.description: Active capacity exists in more than one region, enabling traffic to be rerouted when an entire region becomes unavailable.

tags.label: Autoscaling
tags.description: Capacity adjusts automatically in response to load, preventing saturation without manual intervention.

tags.label: Managed service
tags.description: The underlying infrastructure is operated by a cloud provider, so patching, failover, and capacity planning are delegated.

tags.label: Cached
tags.description: Responses are served from an intermediate cache layer, reducing load on the origin and improving read latency.

tags.label: Rate limited
tags.description: Inbound request volume is capped per client or globally, protecting downstream components from being overwhelmed.

tags.label: Encrypted at rest
tags.description: Persisted data is encrypted on disk, so physical access to storage media does not expose plaintext content.

tags.label: Encrypted in transit
tags.description: Data is wrapped in TLS before leaving the component, preventing eavesdropping on the network path.

tags.label: Has dead-letter queue
tags.description: Failed messages are routed to a dead-letter queue rather than dropped, enabling inspection and replay after the root cause is fixed.

tags.label: Has rollback
tags.description: Deployments can be reversed to the previous known-good version without a full re-deploy, shortening mean time to recovery.

tags.label: Canary capable
tags.description: Traffic can be split between versions, so a bad release is detected on a small percentage of users before full rollout.

tags.label: Backed up
tags.description: Regular snapshots of data are stored durably, providing a recovery point in the event of deletion or corruption.

tags.label: Observable
tags.description: Metrics, logs, and traces are emitted and collected, giving operators full visibility into the component's internal state.

tags.label: Alerting enabled
tags.description: Threshold rules fire notifications when key metrics breach acceptable bounds, triggering on-call response automatically.

tags.label: Stateful
tags.description: Holds data that cannot be recreated by restarting, so scaling and failover require state migration or replication.

tags.label: Stateless
tags.description: Carries no persistent state between requests, so any instance can be killed and replaced without data loss.

tags.label: In-memory
tags.description: All working data is held in RAM rather than on disk, so the component's state is bounded by available memory and exists only while the process is running.

tags.label: Volatile
tags.description: State does not survive a process restart, making this component unsuitable for holding data that must outlive the running process.

tags.label: Durable
tags.description: Data survives process restarts and hardware failures because it is flushed to persistent storage before acknowledgement.

tags.label: Horizontally scalable
tags.description: Additional instances can be added to increase capacity linearly, without architectural changes or downtime.

tags.label: Asynchronous
tags.description: Processing is decoupled from the request path via a queue or event stream, so slowdowns do not block callers directly.

tags.label: Scheduled
tags.description: Work is triggered by a timer rather than by an inbound request, so execution depends on the scheduler being available and the system clock being accurate.

tags.label: Third-party dependency
tags.description: This component delegates a function to a service operated outside the team's direct control, meaning its availability and behaviour are governed by the vendor rather than internal engineering.

tags.label: Audit logged
tags.description: Access and mutations are recorded with actor, timestamp, and affected resource, satisfying compliance audit trails.

tags.label: Least privilege
tags.description: The component operates with the minimum permissions needed, limiting the blast radius of a credential compromise.

tags.label: Secrets rotated
tags.description: Credentials and secrets are rotated on a schedule, ensuring that any leaked secret becomes invalid before it can be exploited.
The node uses direct connections with no connection pooler — under load, connection exhaustion will cause widespread 'too many connections' failures.
tags.label: No connection pooling
